An AI assistant for Mifos X where the officer still decides.

A loan officer types one sentence instead of working through twenty clicks. Nothing that touches money executes without a human pressing Confirm. The problem

The software already works. Reaching it is the hard part.

Mifos X powers financial services for more than six million people through 250 institutions across 36 countries. Every feature a loan officer needs is already in there. What stands between the officer and those features is distance.

Approving one loan means moving through several screens and filling a form. A new hire needs weeks before they work unsupervised. And the system knows a great deal it never volunteers: which repayments are overdue, which applications are waiting, which clients qualify for more. If nobody goes looking, nobody finds out.

Today

20+ clicks

Dashboard, clients, search, the right client, loans, the right loan, approve, six fields, submit. Repeated twenty times a day.

With the Copilot

One sentence

“Approve Meera's loan at 28,000.” Read the card. Press Confirm. The books are updated under your own name.

Time returned to a loan officer is time spent with the people the branch exists to serve.

What it is

An assistant that proposes, and an officer who disposes

The Copilot is a chat panel inside the app officers already use. Four things happen to every message, in the same order, every time.

#What happensWhy it is built that way
1The assistant works out which banking operation the sentence meansOfficers describe outcomes, not API calls
2If it only reads data, it answers straight awayLooking something up carries no risk
3If it would change data, everything stops and a confirmation card appearsNothing has reached the bank yet. This pause is the product
4On Confirm it executes as that officerExisting permissions apply and the audit trail names a real person

The property everything else rests on

What the officer approves on the card is exactly what reaches the banking system. Not approximately. Exactly. The proof section shows this on a loan where the officer changed the amount at the moment of approval, and the design section explains the mechanism that guarantees it.

How it works

Three parts, and one line that must never be crossed

The web app is the screen. The gateway is the brain. Fineract is the bank. The design lives in what crosses each boundary, and what deliberately does not.

The mechanism

What actually happens when money is involved

A read and a write travel completely different paths. This is the difference between a chatbot and something a regulated institution can run.

The proof

Evidence from a live run against a real core banking system

Everything below was captured automatically from one session against sandbox.mifos.community with a real AI model. Nothing is mocked, staged, or re-enacted. The client and the loan exist in the sandbox and were created by typing sentences.

The moment that decides whether this is trustworthy

An officer rarely approves exactly what was applied for. Here the application is for 30,000 and the officer decides on 28,000 at the point of approval. This is where an assistant that is merely persuasive becomes dangerous.

Safety

Shown, not claimed

Every property below was exercised in the same live run. These are screenshots, not intentions.

The full set of guarantees

The riskHow the design answers it
The AI key leaksIt exists only in the gateway's configuration, on a server the institution controls. Open the browser's network tab during a conversation and there is no key to find.
An AI acting beyond its authorityEvery operation runs with the officer's own credential. A field officer who cannot approve loans still cannot, because Fineract refuses exactly as it would in the normal interface.
Actions nobody is accountable forThe audit trail names the officer, not a shared service account, because the gateway holds no banking account of its own.
Money moving without a humanEvery write pauses. Cards are single use, they expire, and only the officer who asked can decide them.
A double click paying twiceThe gateway generates the deduplication reference and Fineract recognises repeats natively. A retry returns the original result instead of paying again.
The card saying one thing, the system doing anotherIf the AI supplies any value the operation does not define, the request is refused before a card is ever shown.
A failure reported as successThe tick appears only when Fineract accepts. A rejection reads “Not completed”, with the reason.
The AI inventing an operationIt can only call operations on a reviewed list held by the gateway. Anything else is refused however it is phrased.
Customer data reaching a cloud modelSensitive fields can be masked per operation. Institutions that cannot send data outside run Ollama on their own hardware and nothing leaves the network.
Acting on the wrong institutionThe gateway compares the backend the officer is viewing with its own and refuses to run if they differ, naming both.

The one thing it can never do

Move money on its own. There is no flag that disables the confirmation step, because the step is the product.

What was built

The frontend panel existed as an interface with no working connection behind it. The assistant itself did not exist anywhere. Both were delivered in this cycle.

PieceWhat it doesWhere
Streaming transportCarries the conversation between browser and gateway, releases the connection on every exit path, and makes the stop button genuinely stopweb app
Conversation orchestrationSanitises input, drives the stream, holds the pending confirmation, and keeps history separated per institution and per officerweb app
Confirmation flowRenders the card inside the conversation and executes only through a separate, re-authenticated decision requestweb app + gateway
The agent loopInterprets the message, chooses an operation from the allow-list, enforces the round limit, and pauses on every writegateway core
Model abstractionOne interface for Groq, OpenAI, Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible engine, so switching is configuration rather than codegateway core
Banking executorCalls Fineract with the officer's own credential, generates the deduplication reference, and masks sensitive fieldsgateway core
Approval storeSingle-use, expiring confirmation cards bound to the officer who asked for themgateway core
Operation manifestThe reviewed list of twelve operations that bounds everything the assistant can reachgateway
DeploymentContainer image, environment configuration across four files, and written instructions for connecting a Mifos environmentboth

The tests deliberately guard the rules rather than the plumbing: that a write cannot execute without confirmation, that a card cannot be used twice, that one officer cannot approve another's card, that the values on the card reach the request, and that the assistant core stays free of framework dependencies so it can later be embedded inside a Fineract plugin without a rewrite.

The web-app half ships switched off, so existing deployments are untouched until an administrator enables it.

Deployment

Two steps to a live showcase

Run the gateway, then point the web app at it. Everything else is merged.

One · run the gateway

git clone https://github.com/openMF/mcp-mifosx.git
cd mcp-mifosx/gateway
docker build -t openmf/mifos-copilot-gateway .

docker run -d --name copilot-gateway -p 8090:8090 \
  -e COPILOT_LLM_PROVIDER=groq \
  -e COPILOT_LLM_API_KEY=<the AI key> \
  -e COPILOT_LLM_MODEL=qwen/qwen3.6-27b \
  -e FINERACT_BASE_URL=https://sandbox.mifos.community \
  -e COPILOT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://<the web app address> \
  openmf/mifos-copilot-gateway

Confirm it is healthy at /copilot/api/v1/health; a correct response names the provider and reports twelve available operations.

Two · switch the panel on

MIFOS_ENABLE_COPILOT=true
MIFOS_COPILOT_MCP_BASE_URL=https://<the gateway address>

Leaving the gateway address empty is a safe demonstration mode: the panel behaves normally on built-in sample replies and contacts no server at all. Officers additionally need one of ALL_FUNCTIONS, USE_MCP_TOOLS or READ_COPILOT, so it can be rolled out to one branch before going wider.

SettingMeaningDefault
COPILOT_LLM_PROVIDERmock, groq, openai or ollamamock
COPILOT_LLM_API_KEYThe AI key. Server side only.empty
COPILOT_LLM_MODELModel identifierqwen/qwen3.6-27b
FINERACT_BASE_URLThe Fineract the operations act onsandbox
COPILOT_ALLOWED_ORIGINSWhich addresses may call the gatewayhttp://localhost:4200
COPILOT_APPROVAL_TTL_SECONDSHow long a confirmation card stays valid300
COPILOT_DATA_RESIDENCYcloud or on-premcloud

The mistake that will cost the most time

The gateway's FINERACT_BASE_URL and the web app's own Fineract must be the same server. If they differ, records created through the Copilot appear nowhere on the officer's screen. The gateway detects this and refuses to run rather than acting on the wrong institution, naming both servers in the message. The web app also remembers a previously chosen server in the browser, so check the server selector too.

An HTTPS web app cannot call an HTTP gateway; browsers block it. The gateway needs TLS in front of it for any real deployment. Full instructions, including a troubleshooting table, are in gateway/DEPLOY-SANDBOX.txt.

Submit a loan applicationWriteRequired
Approve a loanWriteRequired
Disburse a loanWriteRequired
Record a repaymentWriteRequired

Deliberately absent

Product configuration, accounting rules, user administration, and anything running free-form database queries. Setting up a loan product is a back-office decision that deserves a considered screen, not a sentence. Free-form queries are excluded because no officer can meaningfully review a database query on a confirmation card, so approving one would be a ritual rather than a control.

Engineering decisions

Four choices that took the longest to get right

The officer's identity travels with every action

The obvious build gives the middleware its own banking login. It is simpler, and it is what most integrations do. It is also how you end up with an audit trail where everything was done by “copilot-service”, which makes the log useless precisely when it matters. Instead the browser passes the officer's existing credential with each message and the gateway forwards it, holding no banking account of its own. It therefore cannot exceed the permissions of whoever is using it.

The confirmation card is built by the server

If the AI wrote the card, then persuading the AI to write something misleading would be enough to obtain a signature for it. So the gateway assembles the card from the parsed operation, and refuses outright if the AI supplies a value the operation does not define. That is what makes Exhibit 7 trustworthy rather than merely correct on the day.

The reference number is generated by the server

Fineract can already refuse to perform the same operation twice, given a reference. It matters who generates it. If the browser did, a tampered client could reuse an old one and make a genuine payment silently vanish.

Dates come from the bank, not from the server's clock

This one was found by testing rather than reasoning. The gateway ran in India and Fineract in UTC, so after half past six each evening the gateway's calendar had already advanced a day. Fineract rejects operations dated in its future, so every write would have failed every evening. The gateway now asks Fineract what day it is, falls back to the date on Fineract's own response, and never trusts its own clock.

Candour

What it does not do yet

Stated plainly, because a reviewer will find them anyway and it is better that they are already known.

  • Conversations and pending confirmations live in memory. They do not survive a gateway restart and do not replicate. One instance is right for a branch or a demonstration; a durable store is needed before running several behind a load balancer.
  • A free AI account will rate limit a rapid demonstration. Two exhibits above show it happening. Human typing speed is generally fine; a paid account or a local Ollama removes the limit and is worth arranging before a public showcase.
  • Masking of sensitive fields is minimal by default. Only client contact details are masked. Institutions sending data to a cloud model should extend the list for their own requirements.
  • Under OAuth, a token refresh invalidates a card already on screen. The officer is asked to request the action again. Basic authentication is unaffected.
  • The panel does not yet volunteer information. The proactive briefing, where opening a client surfaces what needs attention unprompted, is designed but not built. Documents, credit reports and contract generation are likewise still ahead.

Running it

What a Mifos environment needs to provide

1

A host for the gateway, with a hostname and TLS. It is a single small container.

2

An AI key in that container's environment. A free Groq account is sufficient; Ollama on the same machine needs no key and sends nothing outside the network.

3

The two settings enabled on whichever web app instance hosts the demonstration.

One open decision

Whether the showcase should route through the MCP tool servers rather than Fineract's REST API directly. The present arrangement is what preserves per-officer identity in the audit trail, so I would keep it unless there is a reason to prefer otherwise, but it is a contained change behind a single interface and I am glad to make it either way.

Work still ahead

The proactive briefing is next, followed by conversation history that survives a restart, then documents, credit reports and contract generation. All of it sits behind the same confirmation model, so nothing already reviewed has to be revisited.
